files.content:
# Prometheus and OpenTelemetry side by side, each order counted once in Splunk

One Python service, `orders`, runs as two pods on EKS, one on each of two nodes, behind one Service. Each pod counts
every order two ways, as teams do while they move to OpenTelemetry:

- a Prometheus counter, `orders_created_total{run}` (prometheus-client 0.26.0), on `GET /metrics`, for a scrape job;
- zero-code OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry-instrument`, 0.66b2), which records `http.server.request.duration` for every
  `POST /orders/<n>` and pushes it over OTLP to the Splunk OTel Collector agent on the pod's own node.

The agent is the Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1, a DaemonSet with one agent per node, sending to Splunk
Observability Cloud. Only the agent's config differs between runs:

| Config | Runs | How the agent finds the orders pods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `values-everywhere.yaml` | everywhere-1, everywhere-2 (`reproduce.sh`) | a `prometheus/orders` scrape job with Kubernetes pod discovery for `app=orders` |
| `values-node.yaml` | node-1, node-2 (`fix.sh`) | the same job plus one field selector: `spec.nodeName=${env:K8S_NODE_NAME}` |
| `values-autodetect.yaml` | autodetect-1, autodetect-2 (`fix.sh`) | no job of our own: `autodetect.prometheus: true`, which scrapes pods with `prometheus.io/scrape: "true"` on the agent's node |

Both orders pods carry the `prometheus.io/scrape`, `prometheus.io/port` and `prometheus.io/path` annotations in every run.
Each run restarts both pods with a new `run` label (the lab's name plus the run), so counters start at 0 and every run's
series in Splunk are its own. Every scrape job runs every 10 s. Each run waits 25 s at 0, sends 20 s of open-loop load at
10 orders a second through the Service, then waits 22 s for two more scrapes and OTLP exports.

What is measured, per run:
- `orders_ok`: orders that succeeded, counted by the load.
- `pod_orders`: the orders the two pods counted themselves (their own counters, read in the pods).
- `pod_scrapers`: scraper-and-pod pairs, from each pod's own record of who read its `/metrics` (an IP with 2 or more
  scrapes counts). One scraper per pod gives 2.
- `splunk_prometheus_orders`: the Prometheus counter in Splunk for the run, the newest value of each series summed.
- `splunk_prometheus_series`: how many metric time series in Splunk hold that counter for the run.
- `splunk_series_per_pod_max`: the most series any one scrape target (a pod's IP and port, `service.instance.id`) has in
  Splunk (1 is one per pod).
- `splunk_dims_splitting_a_pod`: how many dimensions have different values between series of the same target (0 when
  each pod has one series). Their names and each series' values are printed with it.
- `splunk_otel_orders`: OpenTelemetry's own count of the same orders in Splunk (`http.server.request.duration_count` for
  `http.request.method` POST and `http.response.status_code` 200), pushed once over OTLP.

Every config change saves the agent's whole rendered ConfigMap to `config-<config>.yaml`, fails if it isn't the config
the run needs, and prints the scrape job, discovery and autodetect lines and each agent pod's node, and every
run prints how many scrapers each pod had before the load and, after it, each scraper IP with the node of the agent that
owns it.

`reproduce.sh` passes when both everywhere runs show 4 scraper-and-pod pairs (every agent scraped every pod) and
OpenTelemetry's count in Splunk matches the pods. What Splunk's Prometheus counter shows for them is measured, not gated:
the chart's `resource_detection` (override, eks detector) sets `host.name` and `host.id` per node, so series from two agents
are expected to differ in those dimensions and add up to about twice. `fix.sh` passes when, in all four node and autodetect runs, Splunk's Prometheus counter
equals what the pods counted, over 2 series with 1 a pod, with 2 scraper-and-pod pairs; OpenTelemetry's count matches in
all six runs; and the everywhere runs keep 4 scraper-and-pod pairs, which ties any extra count to its cause.

`check.sh` is the free check on a GitHub runner with Docker: the same app, packages and load, with two Collector
containers (contrib 0.165.0) that each scrape both pods, writing to a file. It shows the doubling and OpenTelemetry's
single count before AWS. Node scoping needs Kubernetes, so the rehearsal and the paid lab show that.

Run it yourself: two t3.large EKS nodes (Kubernetes 1.34), `helm`, `kubectl`, `jq`, and a Splunk Observability Cloud org
(`SPLUNK_REALM`, `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SPLUNK_API_TOKEN` with API read). Apply `main.tf`, then `bash reproduce.sh` and
`bash fix.sh`, then `bash cleanup.sh`. The lab is published with its article on showmerit.com.

Published location: https://github.com/Abhimanyu9988/showmerit/tree/main/labs/count-every-order-once-with-prometheus-and-opentelemetry (with its article at https://showmerit.com/abhimanyu/articles/count-every-order-once-with-prometheus-and-opentelemetry/). The lab ran from the Abhimanyu9988.github.io pipeline, where it was first drafted under labs/count-every-order-once-with-prometheus-and-opentelemetry.


## How the runs are kept apart

Before each config change, `start_run` in `lib.sh` scales `orders-a` and `orders-b` to 0 and waits until their pods are
gone, then applies the new values with `helm upgrade`, then starts the pods again with the next run's label. So no run's
pods are ever scraped under two configs. (The free rehearsal on a small cluster showed why: without this step, the pods of
node-2 were still running when the agents switched to autodetect, and Splunk got a second series for them under the
autodetect job.)

## Background and sources

- Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1, `templates/config/_otel-agent.tpl`: the agent's `k8s_observer` is configured with
  `node: ${K8S_NODE_NAME}`, so it watches only its own node's pods, and with `autodetect.prometheus: true` the agent's
  `receiver_creator` (`watch_observers: [k8s_observer]`) starts a `prometheus/autodetect` receiver for each pod matching
  `type == "pod" && annotations["prometheus.io/scrape"] == "true"`. The same template's `resource_detection` processor
  (`override: true`, eks detector) sets `host.name` and `host.id` per node.
- OpenTelemetry, "Kubernetes Cluster Observability" blueprint (opentelemetry.io/docs/guidance/blueprints/k8s-observability-blueprint):
  with DaemonSet Collectors scraping pods on their own node, each target is scraped by exactly one Collector replica.
- opentelemetry-collector-contrib issue 48546, "[receiver/prometheus] Implement leader election": running the Collector as
  a DaemonSet with the same Prometheus receiver config makes each instance scrape the same targets. Commenters discuss the
  Target Allocator, hashmod sharding and node-scoped pod discovery.
- OpenTelemetry Collector discussion 9998, "Otel collector deployment with multiple pods result in duplicate metrics": the
  same series appear once per Collector pod, differing only in the Collector that produced them; later replies report the
  same.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, on a GitHub runner with Docker, before AWS is paid for. It runs the lab's real code (the files the
# manifests carry): two orders containers with the pinned packages and zero-code OpenTelemetry, the real load, and two
# Collector containers (contrib 0.165.0) that each scrape both orders containers with the Prometheus receiver, the way two
# agents with values-everywhere.yaml do. Their exporter writes to a file instead of Splunk.
# It proves, before AWS: each pod counts every order it took; /scrapes names every scraper; both Collectors scrape both
# pods; the Prometheus counter carries the run label and adds up to twice the orders across two scrapers; OpenTelemetry's
# own POST count, pushed once, adds up to the orders, with the run on its resource. Node scoping needs Kubernetes, so the
# rehearsal and the paid lab test that.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/app c/load c/conf c/out c/venv
chmod 777 c/out

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
for k in ("requirements.txt", "orders.py"):
    open(f"c/app/{k}", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", k))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY
IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ "]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
COLLECTOR=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.165.0
for n in 1 2; do
  cat > "c/conf/col$n.yaml" <<YAML
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: orders
          scrape_interval: 10s
          static_configs:
            - targets: ["orders-a:8080", "orders-b:8080"]
exporters:
  file:
    path: /out/col$n.json
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp, prometheus]
      exporters: [file]
YAML
done
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== One virtualenv with the pinned packages, as the build Jobs make it"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/app:/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  python -m venv /lab/venv && /lab/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r /app/requirements.txt &&
  /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE "^(flask|waitress|prometheus.client|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|instrumentation-flask))=="'
docker pull -q "$COLLECTOR" >/dev/null

for n in 1 2; do
  docker run -d --name "col$n" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/conf:/conf:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/out" "$COLLECTOR" "--config=/conf/col$n.yaml" >/dev/null
done
RUN=check-1
for p in orders-a orders-b; do
  # Both push OTLP to col1 only, as each pod pushes to the one agent on its node.
  docker run -d --name "$p" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/app:/lab/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv:ro" \
    -e POD_NAME="$p" -e LAB_RUN="$RUN" -e OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=orders -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://col1:4318 \
    -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf -e "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=deployment.environment=check,k8s.pod.name=$p,run=$RUN" \
    -e OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none -e OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp -e OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=10000 -e OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none \
    -e OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=http -e OTEL_PYTHON_FLASK_EXCLUDED_URLS=metrics,scrapes,healthz -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    "$IMAGE" /lab/venv/bin/opentelemetry-instrument /lab/venv/bin/python /lab/app/orders.py >/dev/null
done
for p in orders-a orders-b; do
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker exec "$p" /lab/venv/bin/python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8080/healthz', timeout=2)" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done
done
sleep 25
echo "== The load: 20 s at 5 orders a second to each pod"
docker run -d --name load-a --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e RATE=5 -e LOAD_SECONDS=20 -e RUN=$RUN -e FIRST=1 -e ORDERS_HOST=orders-a "$IMAGE" python /load/load.py >/dev/null
docker run --rm --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e RATE=5 -e LOAD_SECONDS=20 -e RUN=$RUN -e FIRST=1001 -e ORDERS_HOST=orders-b "$IMAGE" python /load/load.py > c/load-b.txt
docker wait load-a >/dev/null; docker logs load-a > c/load-a.txt
sleep 22
for p in orders-a orders-b; do
  docker exec "$p" /lab/venv/bin/python -c 'import json, urllib.request
d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:8080/scrapes", timeout=5))
print(d["pod"], d["orders"], " ".join(f"{ip}:{n}" for ip, n in sorted(d["scrapers"].items())))' | tee -a c/pods.txt
done
docker rm -f col1 col2 >/dev/null; docker rm -f orders-a orders-b load-a >/dev/null   # Collectors first: no staleness marker after the pods go

python3 - "$RUN" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
run = sys.argv[1]
fail = lambda m: (print(f"CHECK FAILED: {m}"), sys.exit(1))
ok = sum(int(re.search(r"ok=(\d+)", open(f"c/load-{x}.txt").read())[1]) for x in "ab")
pods = [l.split() for l in open("c/pods.txt")]
pod_orders = sum(int(p[1]) for p in pods)
print(f"orders ok {ok}; the pods counted {pod_orders}; scrapers: {[(p[0], p[2:]) for p in pods]}")
pod_orders == ok or fail("the pods didn't count every order")
all(len([s for s in p[2:] if int(s.split(':')[1]) >= 2]) == 2 for p in pods) or fail("each pod should show two scrapers")
def points(path):
    out = []
    for line in open(path):
        for rm in json.loads(line).get("resourceMetrics", []):
            res = {a["key"]: list(a["value"].values())[0] for a in rm["resource"].get("attributes", [])}
            for sm in rm.get("scopeMetrics", []):
                for m in sm.get("metrics", []):
                    body = m.get("sum") or m.get("histogram") or m.get("gauge") or {}
                    for dp in body.get("dataPoints", []):
                        if int(dp.get("flags", 0)) & 1 or not any(k in dp for k in ("asDouble", "asInt", "count")):
                            continue      # a staleness marker carries no value
                        attrs = {a["key"]: list(a["value"].values())[0] for a in dp.get("attributes", [])}
                        val = dp.get("asDouble", dp.get("asInt", dp.get("count", 0)))
                        out.append((m["name"], res, attrs, float(val), int(dp.get("timeUnixNano", 0))))
    return out
prom_total, otel_total, names = 0, 0, set()
for col in ("col1", "col2"):
    pts = points(f"c/out/{col}.json")
    last = {}
    for name, res, attrs, val, t in pts:
        if name.startswith("orders_created") and attrs.get("run") == run:
            names.add(name)
            key = (name, res.get("service.instance.id"), res.get("server.address"), json.dumps(attrs, sort_keys=True))
            if t >= last.get(key, (0, 0))[0]: last[key] = (t, val)
        if name == "http.server.request.duration" and res.get("run") == run:
            key = ("otel", res.get("k8s.pod.name"), json.dumps(attrs, sort_keys=True))
            if t >= last.get(key, (0, 0))[0]: last[key] = (t, val)
    prom = sum(v for k, (t, v) in last.items() if k[0] != "otel"); otel = sum(v for k, (t, v) in last.items() if k[0] == "otel")
    print(f"{col}: Prometheus counter {prom:.0f} over {sum(1 for k in last if k[0] != 'otel')} series; OpenTelemetry POST count {otel:.0f}")
    prom_total += prom; otel_total += otel
print(f"counter name the Prometheus receiver gave: {sorted(names)}; across both Collectors: Prometheus {prom_total:.0f}, OpenTelemetry {otel_total:.0f}")
names or fail("no orders_created series carried the run label")
prom_total == 2 * ok or fail(f"two scrapers should give twice the orders, got {prom_total:.0f} for {ok}")
otel_total == ok or fail(f"OpenTelemetry should count each order once, got {otel_total:.0f} for {ok}")
print("CHECK PASSED")
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: two ways to scrape each pod once, nothing else changed. Two runs each:
#   node        the same scrape job, with a pod-discovery field selector for the agent's own node (values-node.yaml)
#   autodetect  no scrape job of our own: autodetect.prometheus=true, which scrapes annotated pods on the agent's node
# Then every run (the everywhere runs too) is read back from Splunk: the Prometheus counter, its series, and
# OpenTelemetry's own count of the same orders.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 830 not_fixed

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done
NODE_A=$(cat node-a.txt) || fail "no node recorded"
[ -s truth-everywhere-1.txt ] && [ -s truth-everywhere-2.txt ] || fail "reproduce.sh's runs are missing"
CONFIG=everywhere

echo "== 1. The one change in values-node.yaml, and the one value in values-autodetect.yaml"
diff values-everywhere.yaml values-node.yaml | grep '^>' | grep -v '^> #' | sed 's/^>/  node:/'
grep -v '^#' values-autodetect.yaml | sed 's/^/  autodetect: /'

for run in node-1 node-2 autodetect-1 autodetect-2; do
  echo "== Run $run"
  start_run "$run" 150
  load_run "$run" "$(cap 90 230)"
  measures "$run"
done

echo "== 2. Every run in Splunk"
problems=0
for run in autodetect-2 everywhere-1 everywhere-2 node-1 node-2 autodetect-1; do   # the newest first, so its wait covers the rest
  if [ "$run" = autodetect-2 ]; then splunk_run_patiently "$run" "$(cap 200 120)"; else splunk_run_patiently "$run" "$(cap 60 100)"; fi
  want=$(cat "truth-$run.txt")
  [ -s "series-$run.json" ] && [ -s "metric-names-$run.txt" ] || { echo "  $run: no series or metric names were read from Splunk"; problems=$((problems + 1)); }
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: pod_orders[$run]=$want"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_prometheus_orders[$run]=$prom_total"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_prometheus_series[$run]=$prom_series"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_otel_orders[$run]=$otel_total"
  [ "$per_pod" != error ] && echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_series_per_pod_max[$run]=$per_pod"
  [ "$dims_n" != error ] && echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_dims_splitting_a_pod[$run]=$dims_n"
  case "$run" in
    everywhere-*) ;;   # measured, not a condition: what Splunk shows when every agent scrapes every pod is the finding
    *) [ "$prom_total" = "$want" ] || { echo "  $run: Splunk's counter $prom_total, the pods counted $want"; problems=$((problems + 1)); }
       [ "$prom_series" = 2 ] && [ "$per_pod" = 1 ] || { echo "  $run: $prom_series series, $per_pod for one pod, expected one per pod"; problems=$((problems + 1)); } ;;
  esac
  [ "$otel_total" = "$want" ] || { echo "  $run: OpenTelemetry counted $otel_total, the pods $want"; problems=$((problems + 1)); }
done
# Who scraped each pod, from the pods' own records: every agent scraped every pod in the everywhere runs, and one agent
# each pod in the others. This ties Splunk's numbers to the cause.
for run in everywhere-1 everywhere-2 node-1 node-2 autodetect-1 autodetect-2; do
  pairs=0; expect=2; case "$run" in everywhere-*) expect=4 ;; esac
  while read -r pod orders rest; do for s in $rest; do [ "${s##*:}" -ge 2 ] && pairs=$(( pairs + 1 )); done; done < "pods-$run.txt"
  [ "$pairs" = "$expect" ] || { echo "  $run: $pairs scraper-pod pairs, expected $expect"; problems=$((problems + 1)); }
done
echo "problems: $problems"
[ "$problems" = 0 ] && emit fixed || emit not_fixed

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-src
  namespace: demo
data:
  requirements.txt: |
    flask==3.1.3
    waitress==3.0.2
    prometheus-client==0.26.0
    opentelemetry-distro==0.66b2
    opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.45.2
    opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask==0.66b2

  orders.py: |
    # orders: takes an order and counts it twice, the two ways teams run side by side during a move to OpenTelemetry.
    # 1. A Prometheus counter, orders_created_total{run}, on GET /metrics, for a Prometheus scrape job to read.
    # 2. Zero-code OpenTelemetry, which records http.server.request.duration for every POST and pushes it over OTLP.
    # GET /scrapes says how many times each scraper (by its IP) read /metrics, so the lab sees who scraped this pod.
    import os, threading
    import prometheus_client as pc
    from flask import Flask, Response, request
    from waitress import serve

    pc.disable_created_metrics()                 # no orders_created_created series next to the counter
    for c in (pc.GC_COLLECTOR, pc.PLATFORM_COLLECTOR, pc.PROCESS_COLLECTOR):
        pc.REGISTRY.unregister(c)                # only the lab's counter on /metrics
    RUN, POD = os.environ.get("LAB_RUN", "none"), os.environ.get("POD_NAME", "local")
    ORDERS = pc.Counter("orders_created", "Orders this pod created", ["run"])
    ORDERS.labels(run=RUN)                       # the series exists at 0 before the first order

    app = Flask(__name__)
    scrapes, lock = {}, threading.Lock()


    @app.post("/orders/<int:order>")
    def create(order):
        ORDERS.labels(run=RUN).inc()
        return {"order": order, "ok": True}


    @app.get("/metrics")
    def metrics():
        with lock:
            scrapes[request.remote_addr] = scrapes.get(request.remote_addr, 0) + 1
        return Response(pc.generate_latest(), mimetype=pc.CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST)


    @app.get("/scrapes")
    def who_scraped():
        with lock:
            return {"pod": POD, "run": RUN, "orders": int(ORDERS.labels(run=RUN)._value.get()), "scrapers": dict(scrapes)}


    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        return "ok"


    if __name__ == "__main__":
        print(f"ORDERS pod={POD} run={RUN} threads=16", flush=True)
        serve(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8080, threads=16)

---
# Builds one virtualenv with pinned packages on each node, once. Every orders pod runs from its node's copy, in every run.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: build-a
  namespace: demo
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 420
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeName: NODE_A
      volumes:
        - name: src
          configMap:
            name: app-src
        - name: lab
          hostPath:
            path: /opt/lab
            type: DirectoryOrCreate
      containers:
        - name: build
          image: python:3.12-slim
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: src, mountPath: /src, readOnly: true }
            - { name: lab, mountPath: /lab }
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -e
              rm -rf /lab/venv /lab/app && mkdir -p /lab/app
              cp /src/orders.py /src/requirements.txt /lab/app/
              python -m venv /lab/venv

              /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE '^(flask|waitress|prometheus.client|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|exporter-otlp-proto-http|instrumentation-flask))=='

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Open-loop load: RATE orders a second for LOAD_SECONDS, to the orders Service, which spreads them over both pods.
    # Every order is counted here, so the lab knows the true number before it looks at Splunk.
    import os, threading, time, http.client
    RATE, SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("RATE", "10")), int(os.environ.get("LOAD_SECONDS", "30"))
    HOST, PORT, RUN, FIRST = os.environ.get("ORDERS_HOST", "orders"), 8080, os.environ.get("RUN", "run"), int(os.environ.get("FIRST", "1"))
    ok, failed, lock = [0], [0], threading.Lock()

    def one(n):
        good = False
        try:
            c = http.client.HTTPConnection(HOST, PORT, timeout=5)
            c.request("POST", f"/orders/{n}")
            good = c.getresponse().status == 200
            c.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        with lock:
            (ok if good else failed)[0] += 1

    t0, n = time.time(), FIRST
    print(f"LOAD start={t0:.0f} run={RUN} rate={RATE} seconds={SECONDS}", flush=True)
    for sec in range(SECONDS):
        for i in range(RATE):
            threading.Thread(target=one, args=(n,), daemon=True).start(); n += 1
            time.sleep(max(0, t0 + sec + (i + 1) / RATE - time.time()))
    time.sleep(6)
    print(f"LOAD end={time.time():.0f} sent={n - FIRST} ok={ok[0]} failed={failed[0]}", flush=True)

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: NODE_A
  enableServiceLinks: false
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: RATE, value: "10" }
        - { name: LOAD_SECONDS, value: "20" }
        - { name: RUN, value: "RUN" }
        - { name: FIRST, value: "FIRST" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi }

# Shared by reproduce.sh and fix.sh. Sourced, never run alone. A run = one agent config, both orders pods restarted with
# counters at 0, 20 s at 10 orders a second, then two more scrape intervals. Runs: everywhere-1/2, node-1/2, autodetect-1/2.
# Only the agent's config differs between configs (values-<config>.yaml). The pods, their annotations and the load don't.
export LC_ALL=C

# Splunk's view of one run: how many series hold the Prometheus counter, the counter's total across them, and
# OpenTelemetry's own count of the same POSTs. Counters start at 0 in every run, so the total is the newest value summed.
splunk_run() {   # run label. Sets prom_series, prom_total, otel_total and dims.
  local s t f
  s=$(cat "start-$1.txt"); t=$(date +%s)
  f="filter('run', '$(tag "$1")')"
  # The counter's name as Splunk holds it, from the run's series: orders_created_total, or orders_created if a translator
  # trimmed the suffix. Whichever exists is read, and the names are printed.
  names=$(series "sf_metric:orders_created* AND run:\"$(tag "$1")\"" | jq -r '[.results[]?.metric] | unique | join(",")' 2>/dev/null)
  metric=orders_created_total; case ",$names," in *,orders_created_total,*) ;; *,orders_created,*) metric=orders_created ;; esac
  prom_total=$(sf_max "data('$metric', filter=$f, rollup='latest', extrapolation='last_value', maxExtrapolations=6).sum().publish()" "$(( s - 20 ))" "$t")
  otel_total=$(sf_max "data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=$f and filter('service.name', 'orders') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='latest', extrapolation='last_value', maxExtrapolations=6).sum().publish()" "$(( s - 20 ))" "$t")
  local got; got=$(series "sf_metric:$metric AND run:\"$(tag "$1")\"")
  jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$got" || got='{}'
  prom_series=$(jq -r '.results // [] | length' <<<"$got" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  # Which dimensions tell the series apart: the keys whose values differ across series of the same pod, and the most
  # series any one pod has. Series are grouped by scrape target (service.instance.id, the pod's IP and port), which every
  # Prometheus receiver sets the same way, so a dimension another component adds can't move a series to another group.
  local by='(.["service.instance.id"] // .instance // .pod // .["k8s.pod.name"] // "?")'
  dims=$(jq -r "[.results[]?.dimensions] | group_by($by) | map(select(length > 1) | (map(keys) | add | unique) as \$k
           | . as \$g | \$k | map(select(. as \$x | (\$g | map(.[\$x]) | unique | length) > 1))) | add // [] | unique | join(\",\")" <<<"$got" 2>/dev/null)
  per_pod=$(jq -r "[.results[]?.dimensions] | group_by($by) | map(length) | max // 0" <<<"$got" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  pods_named=$(jq -r "[.results[]?.dimensions | $by] | unique | join(\",\")" <<<"$got" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$got" > "series-$1.json"
  series "sf_metric:orders_created* AND run:\"$(tag "$1")\"" | jq -r '[.results[]?.metric] | group_by(.) | map("\(.[0]) \(length)") | .[]' > "metric-names-$1.txt" 2>/dev/null
  if [ "$got" = '{}' ] || [ -z "$per_pod" ] || ! jq -e '.results | length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$got"; then
    dims_n=error; per_pod=error                   # no series read: say so, never 0
  else
    dims_n=$(awk -F, '{print ($0 == "" ? 0 : NF)}' <<<"$dims")
  fi
  # Each series' values for the dimensions that differ, so the article can show exactly what splits a pod's counter.
  split_view=$(jq -r --arg d "$dims" "[.results[]?.dimensions | . as \$x | ($by) + \" \" + ([\$d | split(\",\")[] | select(. != \"\") | . + \"=\" + (\$x[.] // \"-\" | tostring)] | join(\" \"))] | sort | join(\"; \")" <<<"$got" 2>/dev/null)
}

splunk_run_patiently() {   # run label, seconds allowed. Splunk takes a minute or so to hold the newest points and series.
  local t0 want e w; t0=$(date +%s); want=$(cat "truth-$1.txt")
  e=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt"); w=$(( ${e:-0} + 50 - t0 ))
  [ "$w" -gt 0 ] && [ "$w" -lt "$2" ] && sleep "$w"   # every agent's last scrape of this run has reached Splunk by then
  for try in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
    splunk_run "$1"
    [ "${prom_total:-0}" -ge "$want" ] && [ "${otel_total:-0}" -ge "$want" ] && [ "${prom_series:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
    [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 + 25 )) -lt "$2" ] || break
    sleep 20
  done
  echo "$1 in Splunk: $metric (series by name: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "metric-names-$1.txt" 2>/dev/null)) $prom_total over $prom_series series, at most $per_pod a target (targets: ${pods_named:-none}); OpenTelemetry POST 200 count $otel_total; the pods counted $want"
  [ "$dims_n" != error ] && [ "$dims_n" -gt 0 ] && echo "  $1 series told apart by ${dims}: ${split_view}" | cut -c1-600
}

# The largest point SignalFlow returns between start and stop (10 s resolution), each point summed across series. A series
# that skipped one 10 s point keeps its last value (extrapolation), so a missed point can't lower the sum.
sf_max() {   # program, start s, stop s
  local out n
  for try in 1 2 3; do
    out=$(signalflow "$1" "$(( $2 * 1000 ))" "$(( $3 * 1000 ))")
    [ -n "$out" ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
  n=$(awk 'BEGIN {m = 0} $2 > m {m = $2} END {printf "%.0f", m}' <<<"$out")
  echo "${n:-0}"
}

# The Splunk OTel Collector chart with one config. Every run uses the same chart version and the same base settings.
set_config() {   # config, seconds allowed
  local args=(--version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace
    --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN"
    --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" --set cloudProvider=aws --set distribution=eks -f "values-$1.yaml")
  helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector "${args[@]}" >/dev/null || fail "helm could not apply values-$1.yaml"
  kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why_agent; fail "the agent did not roll out with values-$1.yaml"; }
  echo "agent config $1: ready on $(kubectl -n splunk get daemonset splunk-otel-collector-agent -o jsonpath='{.status.numberReady}') nodes, chart $(helm -n splunk list -o json | jq -r '.[0].chart')"
  # The config the agents run: the chart's rendered ConfigMap, saved whole to config-<config>.yaml, checked, and the
  # parts that decide who scrapes the orders pods printed. Each agent pod's node is K8S_NODE_NAME on that pod.
  kubectl -n splunk get configmap splunk-otel-collector-otel-agent -o jsonpath='{.data.relay}' > "config-$1.yaml" || fail "could not read the agent's ConfigMap"
  case "$1" in
    everywhere) grep -q 'prometheus/orders:' "config-$1.yaml" && ! grep -A16 'prometheus/orders:' "config-$1.yaml" | grep -q 'spec.nodeName=' || fail "config-$1.yaml isn't the cluster-wide scrape job" ;;
    node) grep -A16 'prometheus/orders:' "config-$1.yaml" | grep -q 'spec.nodeName=' || fail "config-$1.yaml has no node field selector" ;;
    autodetect) grep -q 'receiver_creator' "config-$1.yaml" && grep -q 'prometheus.io/scrape' "config-$1.yaml" && ! grep -q 'prometheus/orders:' "config-$1.yaml" ||
                  fail "config-$1.yaml has no receiver_creator rule for prometheus.io/scrape, or still has the scrape job" ;;
  esac
  if [ "$1" = autodetect ]; then
    grep -B16 -A1 'prometheus.io/scrape"\] == "true"' "config-$1.yaml" | grep -E 'prometheus/autodetect|job_name|scrape_interval|targets|rule:' |
      sed 's/^ *//' | sed "s/^/  config-$1.yaml: /" | cut -c1-170
  else
    grep -A16 'prometheus/orders:' "config-$1.yaml" | grep -E 'prometheus/orders|job_name|role: pod|field:|regex: orders|scrape_interval' |
      sed 's/^ *//' | tr '\n' ';' | sed "s/^/  config-$1.yaml: /"; echo
    # The scrape job's own pipeline. Chart 0.163.1 names the processor resource_detection (templates/config/_common.tpl and
    # the default metrics pipeline; upstream calls it resourcedetection), so both spellings count. With override: true and
    # the eks detector it sets host.name and host.id per node, so series from two agents are expected to differ in those.
    local pipe; pipe=$(grep -A12 'metrics/orders:' "config-$1.yaml" | grep -E 'metrics/orders|- ' | tr -s ' ' | tr '\n' ' ')
    [ -n "$pipe" ] || fail "config-$1.yaml has no metrics/orders pipeline"
    echo "  config-$1.yaml pipeline: $pipe"
    grep -qE 'resource_?detection' <<<"$pipe" || fail "the metrics/orders pipeline has no resource detection, so the agents' series can't differ by node"
  fi
  # K8S_NODE_NAME on each agent comes from the pod's spec.nodeName (a fieldRef Kubernetes fills in). The agent image has
  # no shell, so the fieldRef and the node are printed and checked, and the pods' own scraper records show the outcome.
  local ap fp nn
  for ap in $(kubectl -n splunk get pods -l component=otel-collector-agent -o name); do
    fp=$(kubectl -n splunk get "$ap" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.name=="K8S_NODE_NAME")].valueFrom.fieldRef.fieldPath}')
    nn=$(kubectl -n splunk get "$ap" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName} {.status.podIP}')
    echo "  ${ap#pod/}: K8S_NODE_NAME from $fp, node and IP $nn"
    [ "$fp" = spec.nodeName ] && [ -n "${nn%% *}" ] || fail "${ap#pod/} has no K8S_NODE_NAME from its node"
  done
  CONFIG=$1
}

tag() { echo "$LAB_NAME-$1"; }   # a run's label in Splunk, unique to this lab, so no older series is counted

start_run() {   # run label, seconds allowed
  local cfg=${1%-*}
  if [ "${CONFIG:-}" != "$cfg" ]; then
    # The last run's pods go before the agents change config. Otherwise the new config scrapes them too, under its own job
    # name, and the last run gets extra series in Splunk (the rehearsal showed node-2 at 400 this way). Nothing of a run is
    # ever scraped by two configs.
    kubectl -n demo scale deploy/orders-a deploy/orders-b --replicas=0 >/dev/null 2>&1
    kubectl -n demo wait --for=delete pod -l app=orders --timeout="$(cap 90 300)s" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    set_config "$cfg" "$2"
  fi
  kubectl -n demo set env deployment/orders-a deployment/orders-b "LAB_RUN=$(tag "$1")" >/dev/null || fail "could not restart the orders pods"
  kubectl -n demo scale deploy/orders-a deploy/orders-b --replicas=1 >/dev/null || fail "could not start the orders pods"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders-a --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why orders; fail "orders-a did not roll out"; }
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders-b --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why orders; fail "orders-b did not roll out"; }
  date +%s > "start-$1.txt"
  sleep 25   # two scrape intervals and more at 0 before the first order, so every scraper has its baseline
  local p line out=""
  for p in $(kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=orders --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name); do
    line=$(pod_stats "$p") || continue
    case "$line" in "$(tag "$1") "*) set -- "$1" $line; out="$out $3: $(( $# - 4 )) scraper(s) at 0;" ;; esac
  done
  echo "$1 before the load:$out"
}

# Which agent each scraper IP is: agent pod IPs and their nodes, so a pod's scrapers can be named by node.
agent_map() { kubectl -n splunk get pods -l component=otel-collector-agent -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.status.podIP}={.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}{end}' 2>/dev/null; }
name_ips() {   # text with IP:count pairs: each IP followed by its agent's node, when it is an agent
  local t=$1 ip node
  while IFS== read -r ip node; do [ -n "$ip" ] && t=${t//"$ip:"/"$ip(agent on $node):"}; done < <(agent_map)
  echo "$t"
}

load_run() {   # run label, seconds allowed
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  sed -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" -e "s/value: \"RUN\"/value: \"$1\"/" -e "s/value: \"FIRST\"/value: \"$(first_order "$1")\"/" k8s/20-load.yaml |
    kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$2s" >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=10; why orders; fail "the load did not finish"; }
  kubectl -n demo logs load > "load-$1.txt"
  sleep 22   # two more scrapes and two more OTLP exports after the last order
}

pod_stats() {   # pod: one line from the pod's own /scrapes
  kubectl -n demo exec "$1" -- /lab/venv/bin/python -c 'import json, urllib.request
d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:8080/scrapes", timeout=5))
print(d["run"], d["pod"], d["orders"], " ".join(f"{ip}:{n}" for ip, n in sorted(d["scrapers"].items())))' 2>/dev/null
}

measures() {   # run label: the load, each pod's own count, and who scraped each pod
  local sent ok p line r pod orders rest s n=0 pod_orders=0 pairs=0
  sent=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=.* sent=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt"); ok=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=.* ok=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt")
  : > "pods-$1.txt"
  for p in $(kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=orders --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name); do
    line=$(pod_stats "$p") || continue                 # a pod of the last run that is still shutting down
    read -r r pod orders rest <<<"$line"
    [ "$r" = "$(tag "$1")" ] || continue
    echo "$pod $orders $rest" >> "pods-$1.txt"; n=$(( n + 1 ))
    pod_orders=$(( pod_orders + orders ))
    for s in $rest; do [ "${s##*:}" -ge 2 ] && pairs=$(( pairs + 1 )); done
  done
  [ "$n" = 2 ] || fail "found $n orders pods of $1, expected 2"
  echo "$1: orders sent ${sent:-0}, ok ${ok:-0}; the pods counted $pod_orders; scrapers per pod (IP:scrapes): $(name_ips "$(awk '{s = ""; for (i = 3; i <= NF; i++) s = s " " $i; printf "%s [%s ] ", $1, s}' "pods-$1.txt")")"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: orders_ok[$1]=${ok:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: pod_scrapers[$1]=$pairs"
  echo "$pod_orders" > "truth-$1.txt"
  [ "${ok:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no order succeeded in $1"
}

# Generic helpers: the clock, pods, and each run's first order number.
start_clock() {   # seconds allowed, the result to print on failure. Every wait is capped so a result always prints.
  START=$(date +%s); LIMIT=$1; FAILED=$2; HERO_DONE=0
  trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $FAILED"; }' EXIT
}
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit "$FAILED"; exit 0; }

why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -6; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -6 | cut -c1-180; }
why_agent() { kubectl -n splunk get pods -o wide | tail -6; kubectl -n splunk logs daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --tail=15 2>&1 | cut -c1-220; }

first_order() { case "$1" in everywhere-1) echo 1 ;; everywhere-2) echo 10001 ;; node-1) echo 20001 ;; node-2) echo 30001 ;; autodetect-1) echo 40001 ;; autodetect-2) echo 50001 ;; esac; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: the Splunk OTel Collector agent (a DaemonSet, one per node) gets the Prometheus scrape job many teams add first
# (values-everywhere.yaml): pod discovery for app=orders, no node filter. Two orders pods, one per node, count every order
# in a Prometheus counter and, side by side, push OpenTelemetry's own request metric over OTLP. Sets up the cluster, runs
# everywhere-1 and everywhere-2, and reads everywhere-1 back from Splunk. fix.sh runs the two node-scoped configs.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 820 not_reproduced

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 600)s" >/dev/null || true
NODE_A=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
NODE_B=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$NODE_A" > node-a.txt; echo "$NODE_B" > node-b.txt
echo "node A: $NODE_A; node B: $NODE_B"

echo "== 2. Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1 with values-everywhere.yaml"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1 && helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 10
done
set_config everywhere "$(cap 180 560)"

echo "== 3. One virtualenv with pinned packages on each node"
sed -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" -e "s/NODE_B/$NODE_B/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the builds"
t0=$(date +%s); limit=$(cap 360 420)
done_jobs=0
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  done_jobs=0
  for j in build-a build-b; do
    case "$(kubectl -n demo get job "$j" -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)" in
      *Complete*) done_jobs=$(( done_jobs + 1 )) ;;
      *Failed*) kubectl -n demo logs "job/$j" --tail=10; fail "$j failed" ;;
    esac
  done
  [ "$done_jobs" = 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
[ "$done_jobs" = 2 ] || fail "the builds did not finish"
kubectl -n demo logs job/build-a --tail=8 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\[notice\]' | cut -c1-200
echo "builds took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. orders-a on node A, orders-b on node B, one Service"
sed -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" -e "s/NODE_B/$NODE_B/" -e "s/LAB_ENV/$LAB_NAME/g" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy orders"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders-a --timeout="$(cap 120 380)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "orders-a did not start"; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders-b --timeout="$(cap 120 370)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "orders-b did not start"; }
kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=orders -o wide --no-headers | awk '{print "  " $1, $6, $7}'

for run in everywhere-1 everywhere-2; do
  echo "== Run $run"
  start_run "$run" 120
  load_run "$run" "$(cap 90 200)"
  measures "$run"
done

echo "== 5. everywhere-1 in Splunk"
splunk_run_patiently everywhere-1 "$(cap 200 15)"
want=$(cat truth-everywhere-1.txt)
# The before-state is the cause: every agent scraped every pod (4 scraper-and-pod pairs, from the pods' own records), with
# OpenTelemetry's count in Splunk as the fair reference. What Splunk's Prometheus counter shows is measured, not gated:
# fix.sh reads every run again and records it.
[ "${otel_total:-0}" = "$want" ] || fail "OpenTelemetry's count in Splunk ($otel_total) doesn't match the pods ($want), so there is no fair reference"
for run in everywhere-1 everywhere-2; do
  pairs=0
  while read -r pod orders rest; do for s in $rest; do [ "${s##*:}" -ge 2 ] && pairs=$(( pairs + 1 )); done; done < "pods-$run.txt"
  [ "$pairs" = 4 ] || fail "expected both agents to scrape both pods in $run, found $pairs scraper-pod pairs"
done

emit reproduced

# Low-level Splunk Observability Cloud reads used by lib.sh: series, traces from APM by trace ID, and SignalFlow sums.
# Sourced, never run alone. Needs SPLUNK_REALM and SPLUNK_API_TOKEN.
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
STREAM="https://stream.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

wait_cluster() {   # seconds. Sets cluster to how many of the cluster's series Splunk holds.
  local t0; t0=$(date +%s); cluster=0
  while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$1" ]; do
    cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
    sleep 15
  done
}

trace_items() {   # every span Splunk APM holds for a trace: the newest segment, then each segment
  local seg
  {
    curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/latest" 2>/dev/null | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . else [] end' 2>/dev/null
    for seg in $(curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/segments" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if type == "array" then .[] else empty end' 2>/dev/null); do
      curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/$seg" 2>/dev/null | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . else [] end' 2>/dev/null
    done
  } | jq -cs 'add // [] | unique_by(.spanId // .id // tostring)' 2>/dev/null
}

# SignalFlow answers as a stream of events. This prints one value per point between start and stop, summed across series.
signalflow() {   # program, start ms, stop ms, resolution ms
  curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data-binary "$1" \
    "$STREAM/v2/signalflow/execute?start=$2&stop=$3&resolution=${4:-10000}&immediate=true" 2>/dev/null |
    awk '/^event:/ { if (b != "") print e "\t" b; e = $2; b = ""; next }
         /^data:/  { sub(/^data: ?/, ""); b = b $0; next }
         END       { if (b != "") print e "\t" b }' |
    jq -Rr --argjson from "$2" --argjson to "$3" 'split("\t") | select(.[0] == "data") | (.[1] | fromjson? // {})
      | select(.logicalTimestampMs >= $from and .logicalTimestampMs < $to) | "\(.logicalTimestampMs) \([.data[]?.value // empty] | add // 0)"' 2>/dev/null
}

# Config "autodetect": no scrape job of our own. One chart value turns on the agent's Prometheus autodetection: its
# receiver_creator watches the k8s_observer, which sees only the pods on the agent's node, and scrapes the pods that carry
# the prometheus.io/scrape annotation (every orders pod has it, in every run) every 10 s.
autodetect:
  prometheus: true

# Config "everywhere": the Prometheus scrape job many teams add to the agent first. Pod discovery finds every orders pod
# in the cluster, and the agent is a DaemonSet, so the agent on every node finds and scrapes every orders pod.
agent:
  config:
    receivers:
      prometheus/orders:
        config:
          scrape_configs:
            - job_name: orders
              scrape_interval: 10s
              kubernetes_sd_configs:
                - role: pod
                  namespaces:
                    names: [demo]
              relabel_configs:
                - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app]
                  regex: orders
                  action: keep
                - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name]
                  target_label: pod
    service:
      pipelines:
        metrics/orders:
          receivers: [prometheus/orders]
          processors: [memory_limiter, batch, resource_detection, resource]
          exporters: [signalfx]

# Config "node": the same scrape job with one change. The pod discovery has a field selector for the agent's own node
# (K8S_NODE_NAME is set on every agent pod by the chart), so each agent finds only the orders pods on its node.
agent:
  config:
    receivers:
      prometheus/orders:
        config:
          scrape_configs:
            - job_name: orders
              scrape_interval: 10s
              kubernetes_sd_configs:
                - role: pod
                  namespaces:
                    names: [demo]
                  selectors:
                    - role: pod
                      field: spec.nodeName=${env:K8S_NODE_NAME}
              relabel_configs:
                - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app]
                  regex: orders
                  action: keep
                - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_name]
                  target_label: pod
    service:
      pipelines:
        metrics/orders:
          receivers: [prometheus/orders]
          processors: [memory_limiter, batch, resource_detection, resource]
          exporters: [signalfx]
